- Added guidance to use gladia-using-cli for users with gladia-cli who prefer terminal workflows, in addition to SDK and live transcription options.
- Updated the References section to include links to gladia-using-cli skill and clarified usage scenarios.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only Gladia transcription skill whose network upload, callback, job listing, and delete behaviors fit its stated purpose, with privacy and deletion caution warranted.

dimensions.detail: Submitting local files, URLs, transcripts, and webhook callbacks to external services is expected for transcription, but users should treat audio and transcripts as potentially sensitive data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown documentation only; I found no install scripts, executable payloads, dependency installation, or tool-wrapping behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions are scoped to Gladia transcription workflows, but they could more explicitly remind agents to confirm before sending sensitive media to Gladia, using callback URLs, or deleting jobs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: I found no persistence mechanism, background worker, privilege escalation, credential harvesting, memory modification, or automatic destructive execution.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is coherent with its stated purpose: transcribing pre-recorded audio/video through Gladia and managing resulting jobs via SDK-first examples and documented REST fallbacks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, be aware that using this skill can upload media and send transcript results to Gladia or to webhook URLs you configure. Use it only with content you are allowed to process externally, verify job IDs before delete operations, and prefer trusted HTTPS callback endpoints under your control.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The documented delete endpoint and SDK delete method are purpose-aligned job management features; there is no evidence of hidden or automatic deletion, though confirmation before use would be prudent.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending audio/video files or URLs to Gladia is intrinsic to this skill and disclosed through upload and transcribe workflows, but the documentation would benefit from a clearer sensitive-data transfer warning.
[SQP-2] expected: Deleting a job and associated data is a documented management operation; the absence of explicit irreversible-action wording is a caution, not evidence of malicious or mismatched behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Callback URLs are normal for asynchronous transcription delivery; users should ensure webhook endpoints are trusted because transcripts may contain sensitive content.
[SQP-3] expected: The English language examples are illustrative and do not create a security concern, though examples could state that language should follow user intent or detected content.
[aig-skill-scan] expected: The SARIF scan reported no T01-T09 security findings.
